findings.title: Information Disclosure: Sensitive User Data Logged in Multiple OIDC Provider Implementations
findings.impact: Sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) from OAuth2/OIDC provider userinfo responses is logged at INFO level in production code. This includes email addresses, user names, and potentially other user metadata. These logs are typically persisted in log aggregation systems, files, or centralized logging infrastructure. Any user or system with access to application logs can extract and exploit this PII for identity theft, targeted attacks, social engineering, or other malicious purposes. Affects 10+ provider implementations including Google, GitHub, Discord, Alibaba, Nextcloud, OpenID, IndieAuth, and others.
findings.evidence:
Production code across multiple provider implementations systematically logs full OAuth userinfo response bodies:

1. pkg/providers/openid/openid.go:52 - log.Infof("OpenID userinfo body: %s", string(data))
2. pkg/providers/discord/discord.go:57 - log.Infof("Discord userinfo body: %s", string(data))
3. pkg/providers/github/github.go:55 - log.Infof("github userinfo body: %s", string(data))
4. pkg/providers/github/github.go:165 - log.Infof("github team membership body: ", string(data))
5. pkg/providers/google/google.go:52 - log.Infof("google userinfo body: ", string(data))
6. pkg/providers/alibaba/alibaba.go:52 - log.Infof("Alibaba userinfo body: %s", string(data))
7. pkg/providers/nextcloud/nextcloud.go:52 - log.Infof("Ocs userinfo body: %s", string(data))
8. pkg/providers/openstax/openstax.go:52 - log.Infof("OpenStax userinfo body: %s", string(data))
9. pkg/providers/indieauth/indieauth.go:95 - log.Infof("indieauth userinfo body: %s", string(data))
10. pkg/providers/homeassistant/homeassistant.go and others with similar pattern

All these are production code (not test files) in pkg/providers/ that is compiled into the application binary. The log level is INFO which is enabled by default (logLevel: info in .defaults.yml).
findings.recommendation:
Remove or redact sensitive user information before logging. Implement one or more of the following:

1. Replace INFO-level logging of full response bodies with DEBUG-level logging
2. Log only essential information: HTTP status code, response size, and timestamp
3. Implement a response redaction filter that strips PII fields (email, name, sub, etc.) before logging
4. Use structured JSON logging with field-level control to exclude sensitive fields
5. Consider whether userinfo logging is necessary at all - the data is already validated and parsed into the User struct

Apply changes consistently across all provider implementations. Add unit tests to verify that response bodies are not logged at INFO level.

findings.title: JWT Decompression Logic Error: Reader Closed Before Read Operation
findings.impact: When JWT compression is enabled (jwt.compress: true in configuration), the token decompression function contains a logic error that causes it to close the gzip reader before attempting to read from it. This results in empty or unreadable decompressed data being returned. When a compressed JWT token arrives for validation, it will fail to decompress correctly, causing the JWT validation to fail. In authentication scenarios where proper error handling sends a 401, this could cause all users with compressed tokens to be denied access. In scenarios with poor error handling, this could potentially be exploited to bypass authentication checks. The default configuration in .defaults.yml has compress: true, so any deployment that accepts this default will be affected.
